The high compressive strength of the current titanium alloys is supposedly to be related to the solid solution strengthening, the multiphase structure of alloys and the lattice distortion eﬀects.

The high mechanical strength of the Ti-Nb(V)-Cu-Co-Al alloys (yield strength up to 1430 MPa) is mainly attributed to their multiphase nature and solid solution hardening of the supersaturated bcc-structured dendrites.
The tensile brittleness is associated with the lattice distortion in the bcc-structured dendrites as well as crack initiation at the interdendritic precipitates.

Under compression, the alloys demonstrate high yield strength values of about 1350 and 1430 MPa for Ti66V13Cu8Co6.8Al6.2 and Ti66Nb13Cu8Co6.8Al6.2, respectively, combined with large deformability (Table 3).
